errors.english: Why is it necessary to state that it is not solitary?
errors.why: Continuing the opponent's challenge from the previous side, the Tibetan says the reason why it is not solitary must be stated, not a question about why it is necessary to state it.

errors.english: This very nature of its co-present cooperative conditions, which is momentary,
errors.why: It is the thing's own momentary nature that is accompanied by its cooperating factors, not the nature of the cooperating conditions.

errors.english: a single momentary entity produces an effect that arises in a single moment
errors.why: 'Occurring at a single moment' qualifies the producing thing, not the effect.

errors.english: Therefore, what is the point of the absurd argument that a momentary entity either produces something solitarily or does not produce it solitarily?
errors.why: The Tibetan is the subject of a sentence finished on the next side: 'the absurd consequence that was stated — why does a momentary thing not produce alone, why is it not alone — [is to be understood as refuted]'; it is not a rhetorical question.

fix.find: Therefore, what is the point of the absurd argument that a momentary entity either produces something solitarily or does not produce it solitarily?
fix.replace: Therefore, the absurd consequence that was stated — "Why does a momentary entity not produce [its effect] alone? Why is it not alone?" —

note: Follows the argument broadly, but several clauses are misattached and the closing sentence is turned into a rhetorical question that inverts its role.

errors.english: used with the intention of expressing clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, the individual instances; the plural is used because individuals are meant.

fix.find: used with the intention of expressing clarity
fix.replace: used because individual instances (vyakti) are meant

errors.english: If the support causes the destruction of staying by itself or through another
errors.why: The hypothesis is that the support makes the perishing thing remain, not that it destroys staying.

fix.find: If the support causes the destruction of staying by itself or through another
fix.replace: If the support, whether by itself or through another, causes the perishing thing to remain

errors.english: there is no reason for that functional thing to remain as a support, because that which causes destruction does not remain, as it remains by its own nature
errors.why: The Tibetan says a cause of that thing's remaining is pointless, because when the destroying factor is absent the thing remains by itself.

errors.english: which performs the connection
errors.why: མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is pratisandhi, rebirth-linking; 'connection' loses the technical sense.

errors.english: the fuel (upādāna) appropriation or material cause and that which arises from the fuel—the light and the lamp
errors.why: The material cause and its product are the lamp and the light respectively; 'fuel' is not in the text and misidentifies the upādāna.

errors.english: How that occurs, and how this very transformation, characterized by appropriation, is faultless
errors.why: The point is that 'changing when that changes' is the faultless definition of a material cause.

note: Dense Pramāṇa commentary where several arguments are garbled and technical terms (vyakti, pratisandhi, upādāna) are mis-rendered; inline glosses are also run into the text.

errors.english: it means to be separated from the state of dependence
errors.why: In the context of the saṅghāvaśeṣa penalties (parivāsa, mānāpya, rehabilitation) the root says to help him receive [the penalty] and be released from it, not to leave dependence; the note glossing མནོད་པ as tutelage is misleading.

errors.english: one must quickly be assisted and supported in separating from the injury and moving away from the punishment by the community of monks (Sangha)
errors.why: The pupil should serve and help so that the teacher quickly obtains probation etc. from the Saṅgha and is quickly released; there is no 'injury' and the pupil is the helper.

errors.english: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
errors.why: This states the reciprocal rule: the niśraya teacher (གནས) in turn performs these duties for the pupil, except asking permission (དྲི་བ/ཞུ་བ).

fix.find: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
fix.replace: **He [the teacher of dependence], too, should perform these duties for him [the dependent], except for asking permission.**

errors.english: while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher
errors.why: The commentary says the teacher of dependence need only not ask permission; otherwise he assists the pupil with bowl and robe work.

errors.english: **Not if they lack even one of the qualities mentioned in the sets of five.**
errors.why: The root disqualifies one endowed with none of the pentads listed below (as the commentary's own rendering says), not one lacking any single quality.

note: Readable and the pentad section is good, but the reciprocal-duty rule is reversed and the opening penalty passage misunderstood.

errors.english: The cause of change and the condition of change
errors.why: འགྱུར་བ completes 'become purified' from the previous side: the cause and condition by which beings become purified, not a 'cause of change'.

note: Faithful rendering of the sūtra passage on causes of defilement and purification and the Tathāgata's absorptions.

span_why: The opening sentences on dedicating toward Buddhahood and 'the others in the same way, up to turning away from wrong views' translate the previous side, beyond the sentence that crosses into this one.

errors.english: The (bodhichitta) awakening mind and the compassionate heart of a (bodhisattva) one striving for enlightenment arise while focusing
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks only of the bodhisattva's mind of compassion arising; bodhicitta is added.

fix.find: The (bodhichitta) awakening mind and the compassionate heart of a (bodhisattva) one striving for enlightenment arise while focusing
fix.replace: The compassionate mind of a (bodhisattva) one striving for enlightenment arises while focusing

errors.english: thinking, How does He liberate sentient beings from these three realms?
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར here is 'just as' (paired with དེ་བཞིན་དུ in the next thought): 'Just as He liberates beings from the three realms', not a question.

errors.english: The (aurattika) referring to internal or bodily activities are the actions of the body and so forth
errors.why: 'referring to internal or bodily activities' is an unmarked invented gloss; the Tibetan only defines the word as bodily etc. actions (that cause loss of faith, next side).

note: The lists of 'hundred minds' are rendered adequately, but the page starts with material from the previous side and adds bodhicitta.

errors.english: These are the summary verses:
errors.why: The label closes the preceding verse (rendered as prose), identifying it as summary verses; the English makes it introduce the following prose.

fix.replace: The above are the summary verses.

errors.english: the conceptualization of the sound
errors.why: In this apoha discussion སྒྲ is śabda as 'word': verbal conceptualization, the word 'pradhāna', applying a word; 'sound' throughout misleads.

errors.english: regarding the entities dwelling in that subject, one ponders
errors.why: Those 'abiding in that subject' are the disputants who take it as their subject and who consider whether it exists, not entities dwelling in it.

errors.english: [note: original: (svasamvedana) self-awareness or reflexive awareness]
errors.why: སོ་སོ་རང་གིས་རིག་པ here means experienced by each person individually (pratyātmavedya), not the doctrine of reflexive awareness.

note: Follows the apoha argument roughly but renders 'word' as 'sound', turns the summary verse into prose and misplaces its label.
Faithful rendering of the general and specific characteristics of the truths and the two kinds of seekers of liberation.

errors.english: If that [note: distinction of consciousness] were without a cause
errors.why: དེ refers to the distinction of the bodily transformation (lacking a cause), which would make consciousness causeless; the note makes the reasoning circular.

errors.english: if there is a distinction in the cause of existence
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ is 'as the case may be' (yathāsambhavam), not 'existence': if the cause is distinguished, as applicable, the effect is distinguished.

note: Sound rendering of the milk/body analogy argument against materialism, with two minor slips.

errors.english: what transgression would there be? It is stated that otherwise the fault is a grave offense.
errors.why: This is the canonical question and answer: 'What offense does it become? A grave offense (sthūlātyaya)'; there is no 'otherwise' and no implication of innocence.

fix.find: what transgression would there be? It is stated that otherwise the fault is a grave offense.
fix.replace: what offense does it become? It is stated: a grave offense (sthūlātyaya).

errors.english: there is no transgression for one who engages without the intent for that [note: sexual pleasure] or who acts impulsively
errors.why: The exemption is for one who engaged not for that purpose and in whom [emission] happened accidentally; it is one case, and the monk does not 'act impulsively'.

errors.english: (saṃghāvaśeṣa) offense requiring suspension and a meeting of the community
errors.why: A saṅghāvaśeṣa entails probation and rehabilitation by the Saṅgha, not suspension (a distinct act).

errors.english: is to possess that [note: the offense]
errors.why: The commentary itself explains 'possessing that' as possessing the effort (prayoga), not the offense.

note: Follows the technical analysis of the first saṅghāvaśeṣa, but the cited ruling is turned into its opposite and some glosses mislead.

errors.english: That is not the nature of reality itself. By whom [note: is this perceived]?
errors.why: The root says reality cannot properly be [known] by all who do not see the supreme; the English makes it a statement about what reality is.

fix.find: That is not the nature of reality itself. By whom [note: is this perceived]?
fix.replace: Reality cannot be known [by them]. By whom [is it not known]?

errors.english: Just as an elephant looks back, although
errors.why: The image is the elephant's feigned not-seeing (gajanimīlikā); 'looks back' is not in the Tibetan and evokes a different image.

fix.find: Just as an elephant looks back, although

errors.english: much like a person who is the object of desire
errors.why: མངོན་པར་འདོད་པའི་སྐྱེས་བུ is the person under consideration (the dream person), not an object of desire.

errors.english: who treat the meaning of reality with equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"] and whose nature is free from the characteristics of the objects of reality
errors.why: 'Free from characteristics' qualifies the reality-object that the Buddhas regard with indifference, not the Buddhas' nature.

errors.english: they engage in external conduct
errors.why: This is engagement in discourse about external objects (bāhya-cintā), not external conduct.

note: Gets the gist of the passage on the Buddhas teaching by worldly convention, but misreads the root verse on who cannot know reality and the gajanimīlikā image.
